NB-dn3:
The funny part is that the words may have survived surprisingly well. They were transmitted communally for many centuries and there are several early collections which were preserved separately and agree to a large degree, although of course there are variants, rearrangements, and later additions. But just because the pieces of the puzzle come down to us well doesn’t mean that the picture on the box has. That creates a practical problem.

In DN 3 and MN 56, the Buddha waits until a student’s mind is “ready, pliable, rid of hindrances, elated, and confident” before giving the teaching that opens the Dhamma-eye. What happens when a stage map lets anyone skip to the answer?
NB-room: Awareness as one thing was gone. I was gone. What remained were the room’s flows of colored light, all experiencing themselves in indescribable perfection. They were disjoint, but not isolated: the flows ran into and through one another, connected everywhere without becoming one experience or one witnessed scene. Nothing observed them from behind. There was no cosmic knower celebrating its achievement. There was also no black void. The flows were infinitely more intimate, beautiful, and alive than ordinary perception, while possessing no owner at all.
